title: Japan — Northern Alps in autumn
notes: Fifteen nights, sequenced north to south and high to low so it follows the autumn colour down the mountain rather than fighting it, opening with a night at Nagano for Zenkoji and closing with one in Tokyo. The dates are a deliberate trade: Hakuba's alpine colour peaks late September, the Nakasendo's peaks late October, and five weeks apart they cannot both be caught in one trip — so this window takes Hakuba at its best and accepts the Kiso valley before its peak and Kamikochi in maples rather than golden larch. Happo Pond decided it: reported at peak on 11 Oct in both 2024 and 2025, and it gets four nights and two headline walks here. The cost is Sports Day on 11 Oct, which the trip is arranged around rather than against: the holiday weekend is spent in Nagano, a city, and the drive over to Hakuba happens on the Monday itself, against the traffic heading home. Nothing is booked yet. Every remark on this page comes from the file and is replaced whenever the plan changes; the private notes behind sign-in are yours and are never written to from here.

summary.note: Budget figures are the whole trip for two travellers, in MYR, and are planning estimates rather than quotes — nothing is booked. They exclude flights. The exchange rate is the mid-market rate on 14 Aug 2026 (1 MYR = 38.9 JPY), a placeholder until money is actually changed; every converted figure on the site moves with it. Day costs carry only fares that have been looked up and checked, as a group total for two, so the daily totals are well below what a day will really cost — the planning envelope is this table, not those. Shopping is deliberately not here and is tracked separately; Miscellaneous is contingency, not a shopping allowance.

days.summary: Arrival only — nothing planned, so the first full day starts rested.

items.activity: Check in at KLIA for NH886
items.remarks: Three hours before a 14:15 departure.

items.activity: Fly Kuala Lumpur (KUL) to Tokyo Haneda (HND)
Land at Haneda, clear immigration and collect bags

Travel to the hotel
Haneda (HND) -(Walk)> Hotel
items.remarks: Airport hotel — the late landing is deliberate and there is nothing worth a train ride at this hour.

days.summary: Tokyo to Nagano, and an afternoon at Zenkoji.

items.activity: Breakfast, then check out

Travel to Tokyo Station
Hotel -(Tokyo Monorail)> Hamamatsucho Station -(JR Yamanote Line)> Tokyo Station
items.remarks: About 17 minutes on the monorail from Haneda Terminal 3, then 5 on the Yamanote — allow 30 with the change and the bags. The Keikyu line to Shinagawa and JR across is the same journey by another route if the monorail is queued.

items.activity:
Travel to Nagano
Tokyo Station -(Hokuriku Shinkansen)> Nagano Station
items.remarks: Three services run this line and they are not interchangeable. Kagayaki is fastest at about 80 minutes but is entirely reserved — there are no unreserved cars at all, so turning up hoping to board one does not work. Hakutaka takes about 95 minutes and Asama, which terminates at Nagano, a little longer; both carry unreserved seats. JPY 8,340 per person reserved, JPY 7,680 unreserved — figure shown is reserved for two. No oversized-baggage reservation is needed here: that rule covers the Tokaido, Sanyo and Kyushu Shinkansen only, and the Hokuriku is first come, first served.

items.activity: Check in, then lunch at Nagano
items.remarks: Nagano is soba country. One night here rather than a bus-gap stop, which is what turns Zenkoji from a rushed hour into an afternoon.

items.activity: Explore Zenkoji
items.remarks: 1,400 years old, and it holds the first Buddhist statue ever brought to Japan — kept hidden, never shown. The part people remember is the kaidan meguri: a pitch-dark passage under the main hall where you feel along the wall for the key to paradise. JPY 1,200 per person for the combined ticket, JPY 600 for just the inner sanctuary and passage; figure shown is the combined for two. Allow two hours inside, plus another for the approach street. About 15 minutes by bus from the station, or 30 on foot straight up the main road.

items.activity: Dinner at Nagano
items.remarks: If tomorrow's bus is a late one, Zenkoji holds a morning service at dawn — 05:30 to 07:00 depending on sunrise, led by the head priests, and one of the few daily temple rituals in Japan still open to the public. A better hour there than any afternoon.

days.summary: Five shrines up a mountainside, through 400-year-old cedars.

items.activity:
Travel to Togakushi
Nagano Station -(Alpico Bus)> Togakushi Okusha
items.remarks: Just over an hour, JPY 1,550 per person each way; figure shown is the return for two. Green season runs eleven departures a day from Nagano Station, 06:50 to 14:10, so this is a far easier bus than the Hakuba one. Three things the operator is specific about: every seat is reserved (book online, which opens a month ahead — you can board without one if there is space, but not reliably), Suica and the other IC cards do NOT work so bring cash or a contactless Visa, and the old Togakushi & Zenkoji 1-Day Pass was discontinued in 2025, so do not plan around it.

items.activity:
Walk the cedar avenue to Okusha
Togakushi Okusha -(Hike - 40 mins)> Togakushi Okusha Shrine
items.remarks: A 2 km approach through the thatched Zuijinmon gate and then 300-odd Japanese cedars, many of them 400 years old. The cedars are evergreen, so the avenue looks the same whatever the date — which is the point today, because Togakushi sits at about 1,200 m and peaks late October, so the colour around it will only be turning.

items.activity: Lunch at Togakushi
items.remarks: Togakushi is one of Japan's three great soba regions. Eaten here with sansai tempura — battered mountain vegetables.

items.activity: Explore Chusha
items.remarks: The middle shrine, about 40 minutes down through the forest from Okusha. Carry on another 2 km to Hokosha for the full five-shrine walk, or stop here — the whole traverse is 10-12 km. Use the Togakushi Shuttle Bus to move about within the area.

items.activity:
Travel to Nagano
Togakushi Chusha -(Alpico Bus)> Nagano Station
items.remarks: Last bus of the day leaves the campsite at 16:20 and reaches Nagano at 17:25. Earlier ones run roughly hourly through the afternoon.

items.activity: Dinner at Nagano

days.summary: Over to Hakuba, and an afternoon to settle in.

items.activity: Collect the hire car at Nagano Station
items.remarks: The car covers the next six days — Hakuba, Matsumoto and Azumino — and goes back at Matsumoto. Both are in Nagano prefecture, which is the whole point: a one-way drop inside one prefecture is free or close to it, where Nagano to Nagoya would have run to tens of thousands.

items.activity:
Check out and drive to Hakuba
Nagano Station -(Drive)> Hakuba Station
items.remarks: About 1h 15m, and deliberately on Sports Day itself. The holiday traffic on a Monday runs the other way — people leaving the resorts for the cities — so going north into Hakuba is against the flow, and tonight is the first quiet night in the valley after the long weekend rather than the last busy one. The rental desk will be busy with returns, so allow a little longer at the counter.

items.activity: Check in and leave the bags
Explore Hakuba village
Onsen at Hakuba, then dinner at Hakuba

days.summary: The classic Hakuba walk, on the best date the trip can give it.

items.activity:
Drive to Happo-one
Hotel -(Drive)> Happo Gondola Adam
Explore Happo-one by gondola and lift
items.remarks: Alpen Line — gondola then two chairlifts, JPY 3,400 per person return. Figure shown is for two.

items.activity:
Hike to Happo Pond
Happo-one Kurobishidaira -(Hike - 75 mins)> Happo Pond
items.remarks: About 200 m of ascent, 45-90 minutes each way on a rocky ridge path, same route back, with the pond at 2,060 m and the Northern Alps behind it. This is why the trip sits where it does: the pond was reported at peak on 11 Oct in both 2024 and 2025, so today is a single day past two years of observed peak — and on an ordinary Tuesday rather than yesterday's holiday. If the morning looks grey, swap with tomorrow; Tsugaike reads better in flat light than the pond does, and the spare day is already spent.

items.activity: Drive to the hotel
Onsen at Hakuba, then dinner at Hakuba

days.summary: Boardwalks over four marshes, at your own speed.

items.activity:
Drive to Tsugaike
Hotel -(Drive)> Tsugaike Kogen
items.remarks: About 25 minutes, and the clearest case for having the car up here — the bus to Tsugaike is sparse.

items.activity: Explore Tsugaike Nature Park
items.remarks: Gondola then ropeway, JPY 3,700 per person return including park entry — JPY 3,300 if bought at a Seven-Eleven beforehand. Figure shown is for two. Still the weaker of the two Hakuba days: the Japanese sources put Tsugaike's peak at late Sep to early Oct and nobody publishes a 'good until' date for it the way Hakuba does for Happo Pond — but the 13th is far closer to that than the trip's earlier dates were. Confirm the gondola is not in its late-October maintenance window.

items.activity:
Drive to the hotel
Tsugaike Kogen -(Drive)> Hotel
Onsen at Hakuba, then dinner at Hakuba

days.summary: Down out of the mountains into the castle town.

items.activity:
Check out and drive to Matsumoto
Hakuba Station -(Drive)> Matsumoto Station
items.remarks: About 1h 30m down the valley. Confirm the hotel has parking when booking — this is the one stop on the driving stretch where it is not a given.

items.activity: Check in and leave the bags
items.remarks: Forward the large bags on to Okuhida from here — Kamikochi is much easier with an overnight bag only, and they can go straight through.

items.activity: Explore Matsumoto Castle
items.remarks: One of only twelve original keeps left standing, and a National Treasure. Late afternoon puts the Alps behind it.

items.activity: Explore Nawate-dori and Nakamachi-dori
items.remarks: Nawate is the frog street along the Metoba river; Nakamachi is the white-walled kura storehouses, now craft shops and sake merchants.

items.activity: Dinner at Matsumoto
items.remarks: Local to the city rather than generic: sanzoku-yaki (a whole garlic-soy chicken thigh, fried), basashi, and Shinshu soba — this is one of Japan's best buckwheat regions and the new crop lands in autumn.

days.summary: Spring water, wasabi fields and the Alps at a distance.

items.activity:
Drive to Azumino
Hotel -(Drive)> Daio Wasabi Farm
items.remarks: About 30 minutes, and the day the car earns most of its keep: Azumino is spread out and its loop bus runs on selected days only, so the alternative is a train to Hotaka plus a bus that may not be running.

items.activity: Explore Daio Wasabi Farm
items.remarks: Japan's largest wasabi farm and free to enter. Clear water channels, wasabi soft-serve, and autumn leaves along the streams. Azumino's own best season is late Sep to late Oct, so this lands well.

items.activity: Explore Azumino
items.remarks: Rokuzan Art Museum is beside Hotaka station. Or hire bicycles at the station and follow the water — the local way to do it.

items.activity:
Drive to the hotel
Daio Wasabi Farm -(Drive)> Hotel
Dinner at Matsumoto
items.remarks: Wet-weather swap for today: the Matsumoto City Museum of Art for the Yayoi Kusama rooms — she is from Matsumoto — and the Former Kaichi School, an 1876 schoolhouse and also a National Treasure.

days.summary: Over the pass into the onsen villages, for three nights.

items.activity: Return the hire car at Matsumoto Station
items.remarks: Six days, dropped in the prefecture it was collected in. Everything from here is public transport, and deliberately: Kamikochi bans private cars outright, the Nakasendo walk is point-to-point so a car would end up eight kilometres away, and the ride home is rail.

items.activity:
Check out and travel to Okuhida
Matsumoto Bus Terminal -(Alpico Bus)> Hirayu Onsen -(Nohi Bus)> Shin-Hotaka Onsen
items.remarks: About 1h 25m to Hirayu, then 40 minutes on.

items.activity: Check in
items.remarks: Okuhida Onsen-go is five villages — Hirayu, Shin-Hirayu, Shin-Hotaka, Fukuji and Tochio — and this plan stays put in one. The point of three nights is the ryokan's own water rather than touring the valley.

items.activity: Explore Shin-Hotaka Onsen
items.remarks: There is a free footbath at the ropeway base.

items.activity: Onsen at Okuhida, then dinner at Okuhida

days.summary: Up the double-decker ropeway for the Hotaka panorama.

items.activity: Explore Shinhotaka Ropeway
items.remarks: Japan's only double-decker cable car, up to 2,156 m. JPY 3,800 per person return for both stages; figure shown is for two. Colour on the lower stages, bare rock and probably snow at the top.

items.activity: Explore Shinhotaka
items.remarks: Short marked walks from the upper station, with the Hotaka range across the valley.

items.activity: Travel to the hotel
Onsen at Okuhida, then dinner at Okuhida

days.summary: One waterfall, and otherwise the bath.

items.activity: Free and easy

Explore Hirayu Great Falls
Hotel -(Nohi Bus)> Hirayu Onsen -(Walk - 25 mins)> Hirayu Great Falls
items.remarks: 64 m, one of Japan's hundred famous waterfalls, and at its best in late October. A light day rather than an empty one — skip it and stay in the bath if the day says so.

items.activity: Onsen at Okuhida, then dinner at Okuhida

days.summary: One night inside the valley, as the larch starts to turn.

items.activity:
Check out and travel to Kamikochi
Shin-Hotaka Onsen -(Nohi Bus)> Hirayu Onsen -(Nohi Bus)> Kamikochi Bus Terminal
items.remarks: About an hour, changing at Hirayu. Private cars are banned in the valley; bus or taxi only.

items.activity: Check in and leave the bags

Explore Taisho Pond
Kamikochi Bus Terminal -(Walk - 45 mins)> Taisho Pond
items.remarks: Flat riverside path along the Azusa.

items.activity: Explore Kappa Bridge
items.remarks: On these dates the valley is in maples rather than larch: the maple peak is around 17 Oct, so today is two days past it and still good, while the larch does not turn golden until 25 Oct to 5 Nov and will barely have started. That is the trade the earlier window makes — red rather than gold — and it is real rather than a technicality. The densest larch stands, for reference, are around the bus terminal and Konashidaira.

items.activity: Explore Kamikochi at dusk
items.remarks: The day-trippers leave on the last buses and the valley empties — this is the whole reason to sleep here.

items.activity: Dinner at Kamikochi

days.summary: Dawn on the Azusa, then out to the old road.

items.activity: Explore Kamikochi at dawn
items.remarks: Mist on Taisho Pond and first light on the Hotaka range — the morning the night here was for.

items.activity:
Hike to Myojin Pond
Kappa Bridge -(Hike - 60 mins)> Myojin Pond
items.remarks: Flat both ways, about 3 hours return with stops.

items.activity:
Check out and travel to Tsumago
Kamikochi Bus Terminal -(Alpico Bus)> Shin-Shimashima Station -(Alpico Kamikochi Line)> Matsumoto Station -(JR Shinano Limited Express)> Nagiso Station -(Bus)> Tsumago
items.remarks: About 3 hours all in — a long travel afternoon, down from 1,500 m to about 400 m, where the colour is only now arriving.

items.activity: Check in, then dinner at Tsumago

days.summary: Eight kilometres of the old Nakasendo, at peak colour.

items.activity:
Travel to Magome
Tsumago -(Bus)> Magome
items.remarks: Send the day bags ahead on the Magome-Tsumago forwarding service, which runs in season.

items.activity: Explore Magome-juku
items.remarks: Sloping stone street with the Kiso valley below it.

items.activity:
Hike the Nakasendo to Tsumago
Magome -(Hike - 3 hours)> Tsumago
items.remarks: About 8 km over the Magome pass, 2-3 hours, cedar forest and waterfalls. The classic stretch of the whole route, walked downhill from Magome on purpose — the same eight kilometres uphill is a different day out. This is the day the earlier window costs something: the Kiso valley peaks late Oct into early Nov, so the 21st catches the colour arriving rather than at its best. Good walking either way, and the cedars and the stone paving do not depend on the date.

items.activity: Explore Tsumago
items.remarks: Preserved with no visible wiring or aerials — best after the day visitors leave.

items.activity: Dinner at Tsumago

days.summary: Out of the Kiso valley and into Tokyo, with a day still to spend.

items.activity: Free and easy
items.remarks: Tsumago before the coaches arrive.

items.activity:
Check out and travel to Tokyo
Tsumago -(Bus)> Nagiso Station -(JR Shinano Limited Express)> Nagoya Station -(Tokaido Shinkansen)> Shinagawa Station
items.remarks: About 2 hours to Nagoya — the Kiso valley line ends there, so it is a change rather than a detour — then 1h 40m on. Every Nozomi stops at Shinagawa, which is the Haneda end of Tokyo: getting off there rather than at Tokyo Station saves a leg with the luggage, and is why the hotel is on that side. The second leg is the Tokaido, so unlike the Hokuriku on day 2 the oversized-baggage rule applies — a case whose height, width and depth total 160-250 cm needs a free reserved slot booked with the seat, and boarding without one is a JPY 1,000 charge. Measure before this leg, not at the gate.

items.activity: Check in and leave the bags
Explore Ginza
items.remarks: About 15 minutes from Shinagawa. The Uniqlo and Muji flagships, Ginza Six, and Itoya for stationery.

items.activity: Dinner at Tokyo

days.summary: A last day in Tokyo, hands free.

items.activity: Check out and leave the luggage at the hotel
items.remarks: Standard and usually free at a Japanese business hotel — confirm it at check-in rather than on the morning, because the whole day rests on it. Haneda's own coin lockers and baggage counter are the fallback.

items.activity: Explore Shibuya
items.remarks: About 12 minutes from Shinagawa. Scramble Square and Hikarie for the department stores.

items.activity: Explore Asakusa
items.remarks: Nakamise-dori for the last of the souvenirs, if the legs are willing. Otherwise stay west and add Shinjuku.

items.activity: Shopping at Tokyo Station
items.remarks: Character Street and the Daimaru food halls are the best single stop for edible souvenirs and ekiben.

items.activity:
Collect luggage, then travel to Haneda
Hotel -(Keikyu Airport Line)> Haneda (HND)
items.remarks: About 15 minutes from Shinagawa on the Keikyu, or 13 on the monorail from Hamamatsucho.

items.activity: Check in at Haneda for NH885
items.remarks: Three hours before a 23:30 departure.

items.activity: Fly Tokyo Haneda (HND) to Kuala Lumpur (KUL)
items.remarks: Lands 06:00 the next morning.

transport.mode: Mixed on purpose. A hire car for the middle six days — Nagano to Hakuba, the Hakuba trailheads, then Matsumoto and Azumino — collected at Nagano Station and returned at Matsumoto, both in Nagano prefecture so the one-way drop stays cheap. Rail and bus for everything else, because a car cannot help there: Kamikochi bans private vehicles, the Magome-Tsumago walk is point-to-point, and the long hauls at either end are faster by train.

legs.route: Matsumoto — Azumino and the wasabi farm

todo.task: Book Kamikochi, 19 Oct
todo.remarks: Do this first. Fewer than ten properties in the valley and the larch week sells out months ahead. Half board is the norm — there is nowhere else to eat after dark.

todo.task: Book Tsumago minshuku, 20-22 Oct
todo.remarks: Second priority. Late October is the busiest stretch of the year on the Nakasendo and the houses have few rooms each. Book direct or through the Tsumago tourist office.

todo.task: Book Okuhida onsen ryokan, 16-19 Oct
todo.remarks: Shin-Hotaka or Fukuji. Pick for the bath rather than the room — three nights and the plan barely leaves the property.

todo.task: Book Hakuba, 11-14 Oct
todo.remarks: Three nights on one base, arriving as the long weekend empties out — all three are ordinary weekday nights, which is the point of travelling on the holiday rather than before it. Ask about laundry.

todo.task: Book Matsumoto, 14-16 Oct
todo.remarks: Near the castle or the station both work; Nakamachi is the nicer evening walk.

todo.task: Book Nagano, 9-11 Oct
todo.remarks: Two nights, near Nagano Station — the Togakushi bus and the car both leave from there and Zenkoji is 15 minutes up the road. Both nights are inside the Sports Day weekend, so book early; Zenkoji will be busier than a normal afternoon and the dawn service is the quiet alternative.

todo.task: Book Tokyo, 22 Oct — and check they hold luggage
todo.remarks: Shinagawa or Hamamatsucho, on the Haneda side. The whole last day depends on leaving the cases at the desk after checkout, so confirm it when booking rather than on the morning.

todo.task: Book Haneda airport hotel, 8 Oct
todo.remarks: Landing at 22:15 — pick something inside or shuttle-linked to the terminal.

todo.task: Book ANA NH886 / NH885
todo.remarks: Waiting on an ANA promotion. Times in the file are the current timetable as at Aug 2026; the Oct 2027 schedule should load around Nov 2026, so confirm them before committing the rest.

todo.task: Reserve Hokuriku Shinkansen seats, Tokyo to Nagano, 9 Oct
Reserve the Togakushi bus, 10 Oct
todo.remarks: Every seat on the Nagano-Togakushi bus is reserved and online booking opens a month ahead, so around 10 Sep 2027. Eleven departures a day in green season, JPY 1,550 pp each way. IC cards like Suica are not accepted — cash or a contactless Visa on board. The Togakushi & Zenkoji 1-Day Pass was discontinued in 2025.

todo.task: Book the hire car, Nagano 11 Oct to Matsumoto 16 Oct
todo.remarks: Six days. Collect at Nagano Station, drop at Matsumoto Station — same prefecture, so the one-way fee should be nil or near it; confirm that when booking rather than assuming. Ask two things at the desk: whether winter tyres are fitted by mid-October, since the Hakuba and Azumino roads run high, and whether an ETC card comes with it for the tolls.

todo.task: Confirm parking at the Matsumoto hotel
todo.remarks: The only stop on the driving stretch where parking is not a given — Hakuba properties almost always have it.

todo.task: Reserve JR Shinano and Tokaido seats, Nagiso to Tokyo, 22 Oct
todo.remarks: Two legs, changing at Nagoya. Book them together so the oversized-baggage slot lands on the Tokaido half.

todo.task: Check the green-season Nagano to Hakuba bus timetable
todo.remarks: This sets day 2, not the shinkansen. Alpico run it from Bus Stop No. 26 at Nagano Station East Exit, 75-80 minutes, JPY 2,200-2,400 pp paid to the driver. Green season is about seven departures a day against sixteen in winter, so pick the bus first and work the morning backwards from it.

todo.task: Measure the cases against the Tokaido 160 cm rule
todo.remarks: Only matters for the Nagoya to Tokyo leg on 22 Oct. Height + width + depth of 160-250 cm needs a free oversized-baggage slot reserved with the seat; without one it is a JPY 1,000 charge at the gate. The Hokuriku Shinkansen on day 2 has no such rule.

todo.task: Check the last bus out of Kamikochi, 20 Oct
todo.remarks: The valley has no through road and the day ends early by late October.

todo.task: Arrange baggage forwarding, Matsumoto to Okuhida
todo.remarks: So Kamikochi only needs an overnight bag. Also book the Magome-Tsumago day-bag service for 21 Oct.

todo.task: Confirm the Tsugaike gondola is running, 13 Oct
todo.remarks: It took a maintenance closure in late October in a recent year. Worth a look before fixing the Hakuba days.

todo.task: Buy Tsugaike tickets at a Seven-Eleven
todo.remarks: JPY 3,300 per person instead of JPY 3,700 at the gate, including park entry.

todo.task: Run tools/fetch_weather.py from late Sep 2027
todo.remarks: Open-Meteo forecasts about 16 days. Until then the figures are Oct 2025 stand-ins, tagged as such. Kamikochi has no verified coordinates and will stay blank regardless.

todo.task: Grant the second traveller access to this trip
todo.remarks: Landing page, Who can edit panel, owner only. Until their email is ticked against this slug the whole private side is invisible to them.

todo.task: Confirm who is travelling and fix the names
todo.remarks: Seeded as CMC and a placeholder. Edit people on the Overview page.

todo.task: Pack for a 1,700 m spread
todo.remarks: Tsumago is at about 400 m and the Shinhotaka ropeway tops out at 2,156 m, where there will likely be snow. Layers rather than a second coat.

todo.task: Check passport validity (6 months)
Arrange travel insurance covering hiking
todo.remarks: Happo Pond and the Nakasendo are walked rather than climbed, but check the policy does not exclude anything above 2,000 m.
